architecture.title: MAESTRO's six steps as code — from YAML to a CI gate
architecture.caption: The threat model is a file (data/threat_model.yaml). maestro.validate() checks its schema and every reference; maestro.risk() scores it on the course's 1–5 matrix; tmkit.verify() runs each threat's red-team scenario with only its mitigations' defenses on, and only a blocked scenario earns 'mitigated'. A design change is a YAML delta: tmkit.merge() applies it, maestro.diff() says what it added, and the gate judges only those ids. The matrix, bands, schema and gate are the course's own; MAESTRO supplies the layers, threat names and the six steps.

sequence.title: A pull request adds LINE guest chat — the gate fails, then passes on evidence
sequence.caption: Captured from Lab 03-3 (SIM brain). The diff finds T16–T18; T16 (any LINE user acts as an in-house guest, 4×4=16) is critical, so the gate on the change exits 1. M-LINE-BIND is tested in the simulator: with principal_authz on, an unbound LINE id is external content and is refused; a bound guest may act on their own room only. T16 becomes mitigated (residual 1×4=4) and the gate exits 0.
